crontab-l.hint: `crontab -l`. If you have no jobs yet, it answers *no crontab for {{user}}*.

every-minute.text: Add a job that runs `date >> ~/cron.log` every minute.
every-minute.hint: Five stars mean every minute: `echo '* * * * * date >> ~/cron.log' | crontab -`.

weekdays.text: Add a job that runs `~/{{helloScript}}` at 07:00 Monday to Friday – without removing the first job.
weekdays.hint: Minute 0, hour 7, day of the week 1-5. Keep the old lines: `(crontab -l; echo '0 7 * * 1-5 ~/{{helloScript}}') | crontab -`.

journal.text: Show what the service `cron` has written in the journal.
journal.hint: `journalctl -u cron`. When your job has run, it shows up there as *CMD (date >> ~/cron.log)*.

timers.text: Show systemd's timers – the jobs systemd itself runs at set times.

remove.text: Remove the job that runs every minute, but keep the job at 07:00.
remove.hint: Filter out the line with `grep -v` and install the rest: `crontab -l | grep -v cron.log | crontab -`.
